build: Original English tape supplied by contributor

exclude: Generated video RAM, ROM system variables and channels
BASIC variables, workspace and stack, initialized during play
Generated scene buffer, view occupancy, globals, actor records and compositor depth map

comments.text: Initialize BASIC score, rescued count, difficulty, final rescue count ten, and the machine-code partner state; show the title and choose the player.
Begin a rescue round: set the timer, select a rescue location and its message, draw the interlude, redraw the game panel and enter play.
After play returns, show timeout and restart when the two timer bytes are zero and the partner has not escaped.
For a failed rescue, print encouragement, choose the rescue location, initialize actors and counters, redraw and re-enter play; then test the result again.
After success, increment rescued count sg, read remaining time as a big-endian word, add time*sg to the cumulative score se, and increase the ant divider setting after rescue four.
At ten rescued lives, draw the medal, wait 500 ROM frames, offer a new game, wait for a key and RUN the BASIC program again.
Start the next rescue round.
Read 128 actor initialization values from DATA lines 110–180 into the eight sixteen-byte actor records. Negative values preserve the previous byte.
Finish one actor-data iteration and continue until the 128 bytes have been considered.
Initialization DATA for the player: horizontal position, height, boy/girl-selected sprite base, facing, motion state, spawn coordinates and flags.
Initialization DATA for the partner: preserve its selected position and sprite base; initialize follow, motion and spawn-related fields.
Initialization DATA for the grenade actor, including sprite base 104 ($68) and movement flags.
Initialization DATA for ant 1, sprite base 248 ($F8), spawn coordinates 186/168, height zero and divider values.
Initialization DATA for ant 2, spawn coordinates 184/168, height zero and divider values.
Initialization DATA for ant 3, spawn coordinates 182/168, height zero and divider values.
Initialization DATA for ant 4, spawn coordinates 180/168, height zero and divider values.
Initialization DATA for ant 5, spawn coordinates 178/168, height zero and divider values.
Write BASIC difficulty sp into the divider-reload field (+13) of ants 2 through 5; ant 1 retains its separate DATA value.
Read 25 initialization values into $B420–$B438, preserving bytes whose DATA value is negative.
Continue initializing global state from DATA.
Global-state DATA: initial camera origin, orientation-related bytes, random state and border/event bytes.
Global-state DATA: grenade fuse, ammunition, human health, timer-divider and engine-return fields. Preserve both timer bytes with negative values.
Return from global-state initialization.
Draw the game panel: white paper, black border, clear screen, horizontal and vertical frame pieces.
Finish drawing the lower panel frame.
Print cumulative score se and rescued count sg at the top of the panel.
Print the message-strip background and lower labels for ammunition, selected player/partner, time and scanner.
Draw the upper row of the three numeric-counter frames using Spectrum block-graphics characters.
Draw the lower row of the counter frames and return.
Print one full row of solid block-graphics characters.
Print the flashing retry encouragement above the city.
Show the title before reading the selected character.
Read a key through USR 32912. ROM code zero selects boy, assigns the labels and sets player/partner sprite bases to 220 and 108.
ROM key code six selects girl, swaps the labels and swaps the human sprite bases.
Keep polling until boy or girl was selected.
Set the engine return countdown to two and call USR 32768 to draw/update briefly; then print READY WHEN YOU ARE.
Wait for a key through USR 32919.
Clear the ready strip, run the engine through USR 32768, then return when play ends.
Set the big-endian remaining-time counter to 3*256+233, or 1001; engine updates begin decrementing it before the ready screen is read.
Select round text and rescue coordinates from BASIC lines 1000+10*sg. Apply the retry variant selection, then copy three coordinates to partner fields at $B490.
After a successful rescue, select r as previous remaining time modulo four. On retry preserve the previous r.
Skip r triples in the location DATA before reading the selected triple.
Return when no location triple needs skipping.
Draw the interlude frame. For rescue zero, print the welcome title and the introductory text, then join common initialization and key wait.
Print the rescue score-card header, lives saved and remaining time.
Print the TOTAL SCORE label.
Place the score box at row 12, column 23 by calling line 3700.
Print the round-specific encouragement text.
Initialize actor and global state, print PRESS ANY KEY, wait through USR 32919, beep and return.
Set the first-round welcome text describing arrival at the city gate.
First rescue coordinate triple: 182,243,1.
Set encouragement for the second rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue two; the retry/remaining-time selection chooses one.
Set encouragement for the third rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue three.
Set encouragement for the fourth rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue four.
Set encouragement for the fifth rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue five.
Set encouragement for the sixth rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue six.
Set encouragement for the seventh rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue seven.
Set encouragement for the eighth rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue eight.
Set encouragement for the ninth rescue.
Four alternative position triples for rescue nine.
Set the last-rescue encouragement text.
Four alternative position triples for rescue ten.
Clear the interlude to yellow paper and draw a magenta border in screen character cells.
Retained duplicate retry-message subroutine; prints the same flashing encouragement as line 400.
Print the flashing new-game prompt.
Draw the ANT ATTACK logo from Spectrum block-graphics characters using the ink variable.
Return after the logo.
Draw the title frame and Quicksilva presentation text.
Print credits and Soft Solid 3-D text; cycle the logo ink forty times while playing alternating short beeps.
Play ascending beeps, then print the flashing Girl or Boy prompt.
Draw the timeout heading from Spectrum block-graphics characters.
Print the timeout explanation, score summary and encouragement.
Play descending timeout beeps, then return.
Print the lives-saved summary.
Print the score label and call the score-box subroutine.
Draw the ending frame, set border-state byte $B42C to five, and call USR 36594 for message 17.
Draw concentric circles and the dotted medal ribbon with BASIC CIRCLE commands.
Print TEN LIVES SAVED on the medal.
Print the final score label and medal congratulations, then draw the cumulative score box.
Print a cyan flashing three-row box at coordinates x,y and put cumulative score se inside it.

Enter the engine with interrupts disabled, mark the render list empty, and display initial status. Poll 1 to return to BASIC; otherwise run updates until the return countdown reaches zero. Copy the random-state byte to the ROM seed before returning with interrupts enabled.
Retained creator signature bytes between the engine and input routine, followed by $FF padding.
Read V and C from the ULA keyboard row into movement/jump bits of IX+7. When IX+6 is zero, accept exactly one of M and Symbol Shift: M increments facing IX+4, and Symbol Shift decrements it.
Call ROM keyboard scanner $028E and return its E key code in BC with B zero; BASIC uses this for the boy/girl selection.
Poll ROM scanner $028E until E differs from $FF, then return. This does not wait for release.

Read a sprite ID through IX and advance IX. Select its 64-byte record at $8000+64*ID. Convert the render index HL with $8130, then draw sixteen two-byte rows using destination AND mask OR bitmap. Restore BC and leave DE as the original spacing argument.
Update the five ant records $B4B0 through $B4F0 with $8A5D, passing the player record $B480 in IY.
Allocation bytes $80FF–$80FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Copy the linear scene buffer from $A180 to $AFFF into the Spectrum bitmap beginning at $4421. Copy thirty bytes of each row, skip two source border bytes, and interleave destination scanlines in Spectrum order.
Allocation bytes $812F–$812F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Transform packed render index HL into a linear scene-buffer address. Rotate the index bits into row and column components and subtract eight from the resulting high byte; used by both wall and sprite drawing.
Allocation bytes $814A–$815F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Fill the 512-byte draw-order map at $B500-$B6FF with $FF, eight bytes per iteration for 64 iterations.
Allocation bytes $8179–$817F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

For 512 bytes beginning at DE, test each byte against C. Where the bit is set, write C into the corresponding position at $B500; otherwise preserve that position. DE advances and HL finishes at $B700.
Allocation bytes $81A4–$81AF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Clear the draw-order map and merge six occupancy planes from the view map starting at $B180, testing masks 1,2,4,8,16,32 in that order.
Display message records 4, 8 and 11 through $8E02: ammunition and the two human health counters.
Allocation bytes $81F4–$81FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Load DE=31 before the even-camera wall painter. The renderer selects the entry at $8203 after setting this stride itself.

Draw a dithered isometric wall block in the linear buffer for an even camera orientation. Convert HL through $8130, combine edge masks with existing pixels, write interior bytes, then jump to the compositor continuation $852B, which pops its saved render index.
Copy facing and three coordinates from actor IY to actor IX; the grenade launcher uses this to start a projectile at the player.
Allocation bytes $82B9–$82BF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Select the player at $B480 and partner at $B490, read movement keys, update motion/death state, then choose an animation frame.
Allocation bytes $82D2–$82DF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
If IX+9 is nonzero, take its low two bits, add $F4, and store the resulting absolute sprite ID in IX+8.
Allocation bytes $82ED–$82FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Advance the clear-strip offset at $B44F by $20 modulo $80. Clear thirty bytes in each of 29 rows, with a 128-byte row stride. Four calls clear the four interleaved strips of the 116-row scene buffer.
Allocation bytes $8358–$835F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Advance the four-byte shift-register state at $B428-$B42B. Form the feedback carry from rotated/XORed bits of the first byte, then rotate it through bytes $B42B down to $B428.
Allocation bytes $8379–$837F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Sample the packed city byte for coordinates DE when both coordinates have bit 7 set. Write the sampled byte through IX and increment IX; write zero outside that quadrant.
Allocation bytes $839B–$83AF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Select one of four diagonal city-sampling loops at $8681, $86A1, $86C1 or $86E1 from camera $B422. Pass camera origin DE, destination $B180 and 21 pairs of sixteen-cell diagonals.
Allocation bytes $83C8–$83DF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Select grenade IX=$B4A0 and player IY=$B480. Handle launch/fuse/human hits, update projectile movement, select an explosion frame, then test the five ants against its blast.
Allocation bytes $83F5–$83FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Poll 0, P, Enter and Space in sequence. The last pressed key in that sequence selects camera 3,2,1,0 and its origin offset from player position. Preserve the previous camera when none is pressed.
Allocation bytes $8448–$844F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Retained Sandy White 1983 signature text between camera input and tracking routines.
If the player render position at $B465 is valid but outside the central tracking window, move the camera origin one coordinate step in the player facing. Skip tracking while jumping or falling.
Allocation bytes $8497–$849F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Extract the city view, build wall-depth data, clear four screen strips, project the eight objects, track the camera, sort and difference object positions, choose wall orientation, composite, then copy the scene into video RAM.
Allocation bytes $84C8–$84CF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
When IX and IY have identical horizontal coordinates and heights differ by less than two, clear both motion-delay fields and the IY falling counter.
Allocation bytes $84FA–$84FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Merge walls and sorted objects by depth in the linear buffer. Search the $B500 map for successive height masks, call the selected wall painter through IY, and insert masked actor shapes at their projected indices.
Allocation bytes $852A–$852A, filled with $00 in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Pop the render index saved before the indirect wall call, restore the height mask and continue searching for walls.
Draw the next sorted sprite when the wall search passes its position, then advance to the next nonempty object descriptor or the next height mask.
Allocation bytes $8541–$854F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Load a little-endian spacing word from the three-byte list through IX and advance IX past that word. Skip zero words and their sprite IDs until a nonzero entry is found.
Allocation bytes $8561–$856F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Set IY to $8203 for even camera values, or $8703 for odd values.
Bubble-sort eight three-byte projected-object records at $B450 by unsigned 16-bit index, exchanging sprite IDs with their positions. Repeat until no swap was made.
Allocation bytes $85C2–$85CF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Walk backward through the sorted projection list. Replace each later absolute position by its difference from the previous absolute position, for the compositor depth searches.
Allocation bytes $85F7–$85F9, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Set B=$FF and join the projection writeback at $865A when the projected screen coordinates fail their range/overflow tests.
Allocation bytes $85FE–$85FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Project eight actors from $B4F0 backward in sixteen-byte records relative to camera origin. Rotate/reflect horizontal axes for the four cameras, include height, reject positions outside the 32 by 32 projection window, then emit position and sprite ID at $B450.
Write 21 pairs of sixteen city samples through IX. Within each diagonal increment both coordinate bytes; between the two diagonals increment D, and after the pair decrement E.
Allocation bytes $869F–$86A0, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Write 21 pairs of sixteen city samples through IX. Within a diagonal decrement E and increment D; between diagonals decrement E, then decrement D after the pair.
Allocation bytes $86BF–$86C0, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Write 21 pairs of sixteen city samples through IX. Within a diagonal decrement both coordinate bytes; between diagonals decrement D, then increment E after the pair.
Allocation bytes $86DF–$86E0, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Write 21 pairs of sixteen city samples through IX. Within a diagonal increment E and decrement D; between diagonals increment E, then increment D after the pair.
Allocation bytes $86FF–$86FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Load DE=31 before the odd-camera wall painter; normal renderer entry is at $8703.
Draw the complementary dithered wall face for odd camera orientations. Blend edge pixels into the linear scene buffer and jump to $852B to restore the saved compositor position.

Compare ant height with blast height C and skip ants with IX-style death state in IY+9. If horizontal Manhattan distance is below eight, stun at distances five through seven; below five set death countdown five, clear motion delay and set the ant-blast event bit.
Paint twelve attribute cells of the scanner at $5A5A, $5A7A and $5A9A. Carry selects green (4), otherwise red (2).
Allocation bytes $87F5–$87FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Update actor IX using supporting-block tests, falling count, motion delay and movement/jump flags. Accept walking into an empty cell, raise height when jumping into empty space above, and report landing/fall events in IX+15.
Allocation bytes $8857–$885F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Convert falling count to a motion delay and event: counts two through four report event 1; counts at least five report event 2 and multiply the delay count by eight. At height one also test whether the actor landed on an ant.
Allocation bytes $887F–$887F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
When flag bit 3 is set, clear falling count and resume horizontal collision checks. Otherwise increment the falling count; after its first pass lower the actor height by one.
Allocation bytes $889D–$889F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Set actor event 4, then attempt the upward movement path at $88D0.
Allocation bytes $88A7–$88AF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Decrement the actor motion delay and clear its falling counter.
Allocation bytes $88B9–$88BF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Compare follower height with player height; if the follower is lower, clear its forward flag. Also put the player facing into C.
Test the cell one height above the actor. If occupied, resume the forward-movement decision; otherwise raise the height by one.
Allocation bytes $88DF–$88DF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
After blocked forward motion, require flag bit 4 and an empty cell above the original position before raising the actor height.
Allocation bytes $88F5–$88FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Move HL one cell according to A modulo four: 0 increments H, 1 increments L, 2 decrements H, 3 decrements L.
Allocation bytes $8914–$891F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Return carry as the occupancy bit for DE and height A within the city quadrant, heights zero through five. Height six is empty; other unsigned heights above six set carry. Clear carry outside the city quadrant.
Allocation bytes $893B–$893F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
For height A below six and coordinates DE inside the city quadrant, XOR the corresponding occupancy bit in the packed city byte. Used around ant motion to remove and restore its occupied cell.
Allocation bytes $8959–$895C, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
If actor flag bit 0 is set, treat the actor pointed to by IY at matching DE and queried height as solid by returning carry set. Otherwise query the city map at $8920.
Allocation bytes $897C–$897F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Select absolute death shape $F4 plus low countdown bits when dying. Otherwise choose frames for long motion delay, short motion delay, falling, standing or alternating walking; write IX+8.
Allocation bytes $89C9–$89CF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Run actor physics when death countdown IX+9 is zero. Otherwise decrement it; on zero restore spawn coordinates IX+10..12 and clear falling, delay and animation state.
Allocation bytes $89FC–$89FF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Toggle the ant occupancy out of the city, update movement, and toggle its new occupancy in. Compare old/new Manhattan distances to the player. Turn with the random carry when not getting closer; when closer, animate and adjust facing when distance is below four.
Allocation bytes $8A5C–$8A5C, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Skip an ant whose delay field is $FF (stunned). Select death shape and decrement its update divider. On divider zero reload from IX+13; on other passes run pursuit.
Allocation bytes $8A76–$8A7F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Return in A the sum of signed-byte absolute horizontal differences between DE and HL. The additions remain eight-bit arithmetic.
Choose a cardinal facing from signed coordinate differences between HL and DE, including a diagonal tie choice encoded through the signs. Return the direction in A.

When motion delay is zero, consider the partner following the player. Enable walking at Manhattan distances below six except one; at distance zero apply the climb limiter. Retain or adjust facing to approach, and disable walking outside the accepted range.

Index a two-byte tone/duration pair at $8BB1 using A masked to five bits. Toggle ULA speaker bit 4 after a delay set by the first byte, for the second byte count; preserve border bits and finish with speaker bit 4 clear.
Sixteen two-byte tone/duration pairs consumed by $8B80: delay first, number of speaker transitions second.
Search the five ants for exact horizontal coordinate HL. At the first coordinate match, return if the ant is dying or already stunned; otherwise set its delay to $FF and display paralysis message 16.

A retained sequence repeats LD C,0 and LD A,($B425) fifty times, then returns. It is code-shaped but no direct caller is established by the engine trace; its intended use is unknown.

When inactive, read S/D/F/G as mask $02/$04/$08/$10, spend ammunition and copy player position/facing to the grenade. Use the mask as a countdown, enable movement and a throw event. On expiry start a five-pass explosion and test exact three-coordinate collisions with either human.

Decrement the divider at $B435. On zero reload three, decrement the big-endian timer at $B436/$B437 if nonzero, and print it through ROM number routine $1A28 at row 19, column 20.
Allocation bytes $8DFD–$8DFF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Load message number one, then enter the message dispatcher.
Preserve IX, select the A-th $FF-delimited record from $9000 through $97FF, and interpret its text, ROM control codes, counter substitutions, colours and sound commands.
Allocation bytes $8E0B–$8E0C, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Find the D-th delimiter in the message area, open its stream byte when 1 or 2, and process until $FF. Values $80..$FE encode repeated tone/noise effects; $7D sets view attributes and $7E prints a big-endian counter from page $B4; ordinary bytes go through ROM printing.
Update player, partner, grenade and five ants; read camera keys and render; handle human events, sound events and the timer in that order. The engine loop calls this while interrupts are disabled.
Allocation bytes $8E9C–$8E9F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Return while either human still has both coordinate high bits set. Once both are outside that quadrant and partner state IX-style +13 differs from two, set that state to two, display rescue message 13, and arrange an engine return countdown of one.
Allocation bytes $8EC6–$8ECF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
If both health counters and either timer byte are nonzero, return. Otherwise, when no return is pending ($B438=$FF), set return countdown and timer divider to five.
Disable interrupts, display message 17 for the ending, then enable interrupts and return to BASIC.
Allocation bytes $8EFA–$8EFF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Read and clear both human event bytes. A lone movement event plays footsteps; fall events display warnings; explosion events zero the appropriate health; bite events decrement health and choose its message. Refresh the visible health counters through messages.
Allocation bytes $8F7A–$8F7F, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Before rescue, compare distance to its previous value and colour the scanner; at distance below four and equal height, set follow state one and display message 12. Once following, resolve overlap, choose following input, update motion and animate.
Allocation bytes $8FCC–$8FCF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.
Read and clear event bits at $B42D. Bit 0 selects throw message 4, otherwise bit 1 selects explosion message 5; bit 2 additionally selects ant-killed message 3.
Allocation bytes $8FF4–$8FFF, filled with $FF in the supplied load. Kept as data rather than inferred instructions.

Nasty fall warning for player. Message record 1, selected by $8E02. Starts with $FF and an output-stream byte; the remaining bytes mix ROM text/control bytes with the interpreter sound, colour and counter commands.

Nasty fall warning for partner. Message record 2, selected by $8E02. Starts with $FF and an output-stream byte; the remaining bytes mix ROM text/control bytes with the interpreter sound, colour and counter commands.
